utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Case number IT-97-25-T, the Prosecutor versus Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. A matter has come to our attention just this morning, and a representative of the Victims and Witnesses Unit is here to address the Court. Before he speaks, we would ask that we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to know why. What's the basis of that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: It's a matter regarding the security and protective measures regarding this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that's of some help to us, to know whether we should do what you ask.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. We'll go into closed session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Closed or private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I remind counsel that with the voice distortion, you must turn off your microphone whilst the witness is speaking otherwise the voice distortion does not work.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Kuo: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in your testimony yesterday, you discussed or you described hearing something on the radio where the Minister of Information, Ostojic, made comments about Muslims and Serbs. Did Mr. Ostojic say anything about Serb intentions for Eastern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember if he said anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just before we took our break yesterday you were describing that you saw people in uniform arresting Muslim civilians. Did you recognise any of those civilians?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. Munib Veiz was one of them; Zulfo Veiz was another among others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see happening to Munib Veiz?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that they were beating him at that particular moment and then had him handcuffed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was beating him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, from that distance, I could not see that in order to be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those people the ones in uniform or were they wearing civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see happen to Zulfo Veiz?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that particular moment, I did not see Zulfo Veiz being restrained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him being beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to -- are the two Veizs related to each other, Zulfo and Munib?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they were taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, to a place outside the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That locality is called Livade, but it was the warehouse of a shopping -- of a trading company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they taken after they were taken to Livade?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that they were taken to the penitentiary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them at the penitentiary, and when you say "penitentiary", do you mean the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived to the KP Dom, I saw them there also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a question about Munib Veiz's physical build. Can you describe how large a man he was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he weighed about 120 kilograms at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he by profession?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a salesman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he well known in town?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he known for?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was a leatherwear shop where he worked, and people often shopped there. He was a very nice man, very polite always, always at your service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what day that was when they were arrested?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it could have been on the 14th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what day were you arrested?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 23rd of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where you were when you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at home in my flat with my daughter and my son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who came to arrest you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three uniformed persons came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know those persons?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how they arrested you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they knocked on the door, I opened it and they asked my name and I told them. After that, they entered the flat and said they had to search it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they say what they were searching for?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked me if I had any weapons, and I said I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, did you know of other peoples' apartments being searched for weapons? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they Muslims or Serbs whose apartments were searched for weapons?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly Muslims. Yes, Muslims predominantly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The three soldiers who came, were they Muslims or Serbs?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how they searched for weapons?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them went into the -- my children's room. I saw it because I was in the hall at that moment. I saw that it was very quick and I saw him take a bottle of drink. Another one went into the living-room and asked one of my children to go into the room to be with him as if, "Can your daughter be here?" So, right, I mean she was 15 then and he closed the door into the room when they went in, after she'd gone in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do when you saw the door being closed?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the bathroom. I had been to the bathroom before all this so I was wearing only some underwear. I really wasn't particularly happy about my daughter being there so I summoned courage and I opened the door slightly saying I needed some clothes to put on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the soldiers act correctly during the search?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could put it that way. They were done very quickly. They did not find what they were looking for; they did not find any weapons. But I think that what they had in mind was, rather, taking me away, as they told my children -- that is, me, to get ready because I had to make a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you where they were taking you to make a statement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just asked, "What do I wear?" because it was cold outside. And they said, "Whatever. You'll be back soon. You'll be back quickly."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what you were wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had some light shoes on and some old trousers and a jacket that I found, the one that I found in the wardrobe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reaction of your children when you were taken away?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not react in any way at all. All I could see was that they were concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the soldiers take you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I lived in Ribarsko Naselje, there was the military police headquarters there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when they took you there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed there for a very short while, and then a man in civilian clothes approached and said to sit in the car. With him there was another uniformed person, in a camouflage uniform, and armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they take a statement from you at that place?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We set off through the town, taking Mosa Pijade Street, towards the Cehotina bridge, and then we turned left to the locality called Donje Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the car, did anyone tell you why you were being taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of those, the one who drove the car, that was the civilian one, he said, "Well, what are your sins?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said, "I hope I have not sinned."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his reaction?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said to that other one, the armed one, "Watch him. He's an extremist."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you politically active?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what way were you politically active?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the party that I belonged to, I held some responsible posts, that is, in the former League of Communists and in the trade unions' organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What years were those, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 1993 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The translation came across as between 1993 and 1999. Are those the correct years when you were involved in the Communist ...

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, much longer. But it was during that time when I held some executive posts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I wanted to clear up was you said before the war is when you were involved, but what we have on the transcript is that it was 1993 to 1999, and I believe that's after the war. So I would like to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think the clarification is he said he was politically active before the war but he didn't hold office until 1993 to 1999. That's what he said. If you feel that that needs clarification, you go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I suspect that's an error. That's why I wanted to ask him the follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get the years --

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was a slip. It was 1983 to 1989.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's not a clarification, that's a correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I wanted to clarify if it was a correction or not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they take you that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those persons brought me in front of the former penitentiary/reformatory, that is, the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever been to the KP Dom before?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what capacity?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had some business with the staff of the KP Dom. It had to do with official business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken there that day, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reception room of the KP Dom, where those two who had brought me turned me over to the prison guards. And then they took me to the compound of the prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody register you that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps they did. I was not told anything; I was simply taken into Room 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody take a statement from you that first day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they eventually take a statement from you at some point?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was some days later. We were coming back from breakfast, I and Witness FWS-66. And he used the nickname of Milorad Krnojelac, Mico, and that we should make a statement, because we heard that other people were making their statements. And we hoped that after we had given these statements we would be allowed to go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know Milorad Krnojelac and, indeed, know his nickname?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him because he was a teacher in the Veselin Maslesa elementary school. And we also cooperated in the party, because I held some offices in the town and he was the secretary of the basic organisation of the same party in the school that he worked in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "party," do you mean the Communist Party?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of any other political party?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me? You mean me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. My question was --

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Milorad Krnojelac was a member of another party, other than the Communist, when you knew him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you speak with him and ask him if you could have your statement taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard that he was a person to whom one could apply to be sent for interrogation with the investigator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did you learn this?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From those who were brought to the prison before us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean other detainees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn anything from guards about Milorad Krnojelac's position in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we had to apply to them first in order to establish communication with Milorad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say you had to apply to them, what exactly did you need to do to establish an audience with Milorad Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had to announce to the prison guard that we would like to visit the warden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you ask the guards to speak to the warden?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my detention it was on several occasions, but I must say that I never had an opportunity of being received by the warden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Guards confirmed to you that Milorad Krnojelac was the warden?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why it was they who told us that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Milorad Krnojelac in the yard, what exactly did you say to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only asked him if we could get to the administrative building as quickly as possible and make those statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his reaction when you told him that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I'll see." And a few days later, we were indeed received in the administrative building and we did make our statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we get to your statements, were -- you mentioned FWS-66 also made that request at the same time you did. Were there other detainees present who also were trying to make requests of Milorad Krnojelac at the same time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be received to give statements, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. My understanding is that a group of detainees was walking from the quarters to the canteen or back and that's how you encountered Milorad Krnojelac; right? And my question is: Were other detainees making other requests at the same time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not see anything like that because what we wanted was since we knew Milorad as Mico, we wanted to get an opportunity for ourselves to go and make our statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said a few days later you actually were called to make a statement. Where were you called to make the statement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the premises of the administrative building, on the second floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who conducted the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was questioned by Zoran Vladicic and he used to be an inspector in the former police in Foca, in the former Secretariat for the Interior in Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he wearing a uniform when he interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those the clothes that he would have worn as a police inspector?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, roughly it was a leather-jacket and jeans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kinds of questions did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that it did not take long the whole thing. He took my -- he noted down my particulars, asked me where I was during the combat operations, what did I do during that period of time and I think not much more than that because it was a very, very short statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he treat you correctly?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You could say that it was correct except that he wanted to say something about the fire brigade's station, something like, "Well, there were some problems there, but it's got nothing to do with you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign the statement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He first, and that was very correct, indeed, he allowed me to read the text of the statement. I signed it, and he said, "That's it, you can go back."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you sent back to?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Oh, Room 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told at that point why you were at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you released from KP Dom after you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you released from KP Dom finally?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 5th of October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your time at the KP Dom, did you ever see Milorad Krnojelac again?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could see through the windows of the rooms that we were kept in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What could you see?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that time, there were different types of activities such as, for instance, going for meals: breakfast, lunch, dinner. That was in the canteen in the administrative building, and they went to another canteen which was above us so that practically we could see some personnel in the administrative building on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you saw "them" going to the canteen, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staff from the administrative building and naturally Milorad was among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would you see him walking to the canteen?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said so. They had their dining-room there and they needed to go there at least three times a day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Milorad Krnojelac, what was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was when we asked him, when we asked if we could make our statements, at that time he was wearing an olive-green/grey uniform. I don't remember if he had any weapon on him. I really cannot say anything about that. On other occasions, we could see him in a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Milorad Krnojelac using an office in the KP Dom premises?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could. From the room in which we were, we could see that he was in a room which earlier served for the reception and distribution of parcels for the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I would like to have this witness shown Exhibit 6/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you identify which room you are referring to as the office that Milorad Krnojelac used? First I should ask you on what floor it was.

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the ground floor of the administrative building. It is rather an unusual view of that -- it's not easy to find my way around it, but it's -- it should be somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Let the record reflect that the witness has pointed to a room that is immediately to the right of the place that has previously been identified as the entrance into the KP Dom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. My learned friend pointed, or at least for the transcript, she said that it was only a room to the right of the entrance but not which one. It was the first one to the right. Excuse me then, I did not hear it. If it is to the right or it is to the left, it cannot be the first room to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What she said was, "Let the record reflect that the witness has pointed to a room that is immediately to the right of the place that has previously been identified as the entrance into the KP Dom," and that seems to me to be correct. The entrance into the KP Dom, there's the main entrance into the administrative building, and you proceed through into the interior part of the KP Dom. This one which is on the English version called just "office" is the first room to the right of that. Is there some problem with that description?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I was looking at the ground plan. I cannot both follow the transcript and the drawing, and it sounded to me too vague but now it has been clarified. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need this diagram anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, were you actually able to see Mr. Krnojelac inside that office?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have just said we often stood by the windows even though the guards tried to prohibit it. But we could, from time to time, see Milorad through the window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see him doing inside the office?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not see that personally because I wasn't that close often enough to be able to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn that he was in that office?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was some prisoners who had had an opportunity to go to the administrative building on some business, and they told us that he worked there, that he -- that that is where he was, in point of fact. If there would be some communication between some of the prisoners who had applied for reception then, again, it would take place in that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the detainees in your room tell you that from the room they saw Mr. Krnojelac in the office you pointed out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some could. Those who were in nearer rooms than ours was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those prisoners describe what he was doing, what they were able to see him doing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I don't think they could do that because at that time, all it came down to was sitting on his part and perhaps talking. Whether it was business, whether it was a diary or agenda or something, I cannot say because I was not there. I do not think it was a conventional office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if he was in that office during the day or during the night?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can talk about is what happened during the day [Realtime transcript read in error "night"]. But at night, perhaps something that went on in the evening hours, but not all that late.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Krnojelac on any other occasions? You've described seeing him walking to and from the canteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Your Honour, excuse me, but I am worried, as the transcript, on page [sic] 19, it says, "... during the night" and it should say "during the day." I still remember what you told me, that all this is checked, but I'm nevertheless worried so I had to react.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Whereabouts on page 19 do you say there's some error? We're up to page 28 already.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the 28th page, line 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, line 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And you say he said day and not night?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he would see him during the day, and sometimes in late afternoon but not late.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in the early hours of the evening but not late. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Kuo, you'd better check it out with the witness, would you? THE COURT REPORTER: It was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes. My recollection is he also said "day."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I can ask you, because the transcript shows differently, when did Mr. Krnojelac use that office? Was it during the daytime or during the night-time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lights in that office would be on all day and night, and so one could see him during the day due to the daylight and sometimes in the evening hours. But I cannot affirm that it was in the late evening hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I see that it is 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll have to keep the same timetable, otherwise we'll throw it out for the rest of the day. We'll adjourn now until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember giving a statement to investigators from the Office of the Prosecution in January of 1999 about what happened to you in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember being asked some questions about the office that Krnojelac used in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to put part of the statement to you and ask you for an explanation. In that statement, you described that when you go into the metal door from the courtyard -- I'm sorry. You described the office and that there were bars on the window, and you said, "I could only recognise Krnojelac if he was directly near his window and facing us, or when our lights were off at night and Krnojelac had his lights on." Did you make that statement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stand by it. But I repeat: It was in the early hours of the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I wanted to clarify was that you actually saw Krnojelac in that office and did not just hear it from other detainees.

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any members of your family try to contact you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife spared no effort trying to use some connections, my friends who were Serbs, and she tried very hard to get through to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she succeed in getting through to you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She managed to see me twice for a very short period of time in that part near the entrance into the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were those visits arranged?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period the prison administration allowed visits to us, the prisoners; however, that was only for two or three times during a short period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were visits to you and other detainees stopped or prohibited?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was at the very outset. By the second half of May at the latest, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions about the rooms that you were in. You mentioned that you were taken to Room 15. How long were you in that room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the end of August, beginning of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you moved then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I and the rest who happened to be there were transferred to the other part of the building. That was Room 22.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the witness come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Would you mind moving your chair closer to the microphone. It's difficult to hear you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'd like to have the witness shown 6/1 again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that you and other detainees were moved from one building, I think, to another, can you describe what building you were moved from and then the building you were moved to?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is building 1 where we stayed later. Then, we were transferred to building 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And for the record, the building 1 is indicated on Exhibit 6/1 as building 1 as well as building 2 also labelled as such. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, regarding the movement of the detainees from the building to the other, are you saying that all the detainees in building 1 were moved to building 2?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that period, all were transferred to building 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any reason given to you for that transfer?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you -- and how long did you stay in that second building in the room that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not remember the exact date but, again, from building 2, we were transferred to building 1 yet again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you some questions about your living conditions. What kind of food were you allowed to have?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, the food was truly disastrous. In perhaps less than two months' time, we lost lots of weight. I must say that in that period, I lost 33 kilograms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did the food get better if ever?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one could take the period from mid-1993 when we felt that the treatment in terms of food was getting better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you allowed communication with the outside world?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to receive any news from the outside world?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officially, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Unofficially, were you able to receive news, for instance, via radio?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Actually, until the 14th of August, 1992, we could follow certain events because in that room of ours, Room 15, we actually had a small transistor radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on August 14th, 1992 to that radio?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then somebody, to use the jargon, squealed on us and the authorities found out that we had a radio that we were listening to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when they found out about the radio?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A large number of prison guards barged into our room, and I must say that they searched it in a brutal way. They searched the premises, our personal belongings, the beds on which we were lying, and us personally, the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they take the radio away?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any further punishment for that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Measures were taken by the administration to investigate who listened to the radio and who listened to the news and whether this news was carried to other rooms as well. Then these investigations by the prison authorities continued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if anybody was punished specifically for that incident?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course there was punishment. People were transferred to these solitary confinement cells where prisoners were beaten and mistreated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever taken to solitary confinement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in solitary confinement twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first time you were taken to solitary confinement, can you tell us what the reason was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time was sometime in December 1992 together with person FWS-111. We tried to get some hot water from the kitchen so that we could get a proper wash so that we could wash ourselves a bit, and also do a bit of our laundry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any other access to hot water other than asking from the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the way to get hot water. That is where food was prepared, and that is where the hot water was, primarily for the food that was being prepared in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever got hot water that way before?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In certain periods, because there were no bathrooms, that water was given so that the prisoners could get a wash.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened on this particular occasion when you and the other detainee asked for hot water from the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we asked the cook for some hot water, he said, "Yes, fine, take it." However, then the prison guard came and said, "Why are you taking hot water?" Then we said, "The cook let us do it." Then he asked the cook, he said, "Did you give them permission?" The cook said, "No," and then he took us to a prison cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The prison cell you were taken to, was that one of the solitary confinement cells?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and FWS-111 share a cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were there together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you in that cell together?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that cold night - we were told that the temperature was 20 or 25 degrees below zero - we were there from 5.00 or 5.30 in the evening until about 7.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it like for you in that solitary confinement cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exceptionally cold. We got a very small blanket that we could use as a cover; however, since this is a room made of concrete, we could not get any sleep. We were massaging ourselves, and we really had trouble making it through to the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you become sick as a result of that evening, that night spent in the cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did suffer the effects of that. My health was rather poor even before I came to that room, so for seven or eight days I was very sick. I lay sick, and thanks to two doctors who had some pills on them, I managed to recuperate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us now about the second time that you were placed in the solitary confinement cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second time I was actually already engaged for work duty, and I availed myself of an opportunity when other prisoners were going to town, to the city hospital, in order to get medicine from them. I gave them a note; however, when these prisoners leave the premises, they have to be searched, and the guard searching them found this note. They said that it was my note, and then Savo Todovic called me in for questioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of that incident, how many days did you spend in the solitary confinement cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said to me immediately that I would be in solitary confinement for ten days but that I had to work during those ten days as well; however, I stayed for five days only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you were placed in the solitary confinement cells at night, and in the daytime you worked; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this incident occur?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that date well. That is the 31st of August, 1993; that is the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why are you so certain about that date?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my wife's birthday so I could remember it easily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned that you had been placed on work duty by that time. When did you begin to be placed on work duty?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some prisoners started quite early. Unfortunately, I was not given that possibility until mid-1993, sometime around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said unfortunately you were not given the opportunity. Why did you want to work?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because those who worked had the possibility of getting somewhat better food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to get work duty before you were actually assigned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were in a special position, about 15 of us; we were separated from the rest. I don't know what intentions they had, but the fact remained that we were isolated and we were not given the possibility of going on work duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say 15 of you, what did the 15 of you have in common that was different from the other detainees, as far as you can tell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not really define that. I could only say that among this group were intellectuals, doctors, engineers, teachers, other such professions. Perhaps what I could notice in that group was that one could say that these were eminent citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other detainees who were placed on work duty, where did they work?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some worked within the prison compound, and others worked in town; they were involved in agriculture. And some were in the mine, the brown coal mine, which was about 10 to 12 kilometres out of town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which work duty were you assigned to eventually?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the furniture factory, within the prison compound, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were detained at the KP Dom, did the Red Cross come to visit?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very outset, sometime in May 1992, there was an attempt made by the Red Cross and BBC television to pay a visit to the prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see what happened when the Red Cross attempted to make this visit?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course we were all curious and we tried to see through the windows what was going on. The BBC television people tried to hand out cigarettes. It was a very embarrassing situation, as far as these cigarettes were concerned. You could see hands, arms, stretched out through windows, people trying to get these cigarettes. But then the Red Cross tried to register the prisoners too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when they tried to register the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavko Koroman, a retired policeman from the KP Dom, acting on someone's orders, with the assistance of Mitar Rasevic, commander of the shift, stopped the Red Cross and BBC people from working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did the Red Cross leave without registering people that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We found out later that all of the materials involved in the registration of prisoners were taken away. Somebody said that it happened outside the administration building, but whether the prison administration had something to do with it, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify when you said "taken away", these papers were taken away from whom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the representatives of the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the next time the International Red Cross came to KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost a year went by, the 23rd of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mean that? Was that an error? You said it was the 23rd of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said 1992, but I meant 1993. 1993. 1993 is the year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave to the investigators of the Prosecutor's office, do you remember that you gave the date 23rd of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do apologise indeed. It was the 23rd of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on at that date?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise for these oversights, but that is the exact date. We remember it because on that day, we, from Room 15, were hidden in the city bakery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you hidden there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the prison guards came, unlocked the room and said that we should get ready because we were going somewhere very quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is this bakery located?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right by the KP Dom, about 80 or 100 metres away only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told why you were taken there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not. We were actually told that we would go there to do something because prisoners had gone there before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the bakery, what were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this man who works there says, "Why did they bring so many of you? I don't need so many people today."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of you brought back at that point?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were outside for a long time. During that period, we managed to see vehicles of the International Red Cross that were moving towards the administration of the KP Dom. Then orders were issued to have us locked up in the basement of the bakery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you locked up in that basement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until about 8.30 or 9.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then they came with the same vehicle that had brought us there and they took us back to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn from the other detainees who had stayed in the KP Dom during that time what happened while you were hidden in the basement of the bakery? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the Red Cross had been authorised, I suppose, by the administration, to get in, then they registered the remaining prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you registered by the Red Cross that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When -- were you ever registered with the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened after five, that is, altogether six times, when our group was taken away and hidden, and it took some half a year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the five or six -- you said that five additional times, so six total times that you were hidden; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the same group of 15 people who were hidden each of those six times?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same by and large except that some changes had taken place in the meantime, that is, some men from the group had been taken for alleged exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you finally registered with the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be the 14th of September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know about the -- just to finish -- do you remember the next date that you were hidden by [sic] the Red Cross? You mentioned the 23rd of June 1993, when was the next time, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I remember, the Red Cross next came in August, sometime in the early days of August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember the time after that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult to retain dates in one's memory, but it was every month, month and a half or so that the Red Cross would come and try to fulfil their mission. Whenever they came, we would be hidden. So it happened not only at the bakery, but also in the interior part of the KP Dom, and also at the business premises of the KP Dom some two or three kilometres away from the compound itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, during the time that you were detained at KP Dom, were there also Serb prisoners detained there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first arrived at KP Dom in April 1993, do you know approximately how many Serb prisoners were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you say 1993?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, my mistake. I meant 1992, when you arrived. Do you know how many Serb prisoners there were?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very few, I'd say. There were some who had stayed over, I mean earlier inmates, and very few who were brought by Serb authorities, I suppose, to serve a term or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the numbers of those Serb prisoners increase during your time there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a time period when the numbers increased greatly or was it a steady stream?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were constantly coming and going, I suppose, depending on the situation on the front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say depending on the situation on the front, what do you mean? What effect did that have on the numbers of the Serb prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to certain -- to some information, some of them, I guess, tried to dodge the military obligation. Some perhaps turned up at the front line drunk so they would be brought down. Some committed crimes. Some committed murders so that would be how they got to KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell whether the convicted Serb prisoners were kept separate from the Serb prisoners who had something to do with the military, as you describe; either tried to evade serving in the armed forces or who had shown up drunk, let's say, when they were supposed to be on duty? Were those groups of prisoners kept separate, as far as you could tell, or were all the Serb prisoners kept together?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all kept together, except that some of them were uniformed and some wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and other Muslim detainees have contact with these Serb prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not easy to communicate, but those who were under work obligation, they could communicate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Through these communications, what did you learn about the living conditions of the Serb prisoners compared to the Muslim detainees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the point of view of the media, they were in a better position. They could be informed because they had television, they had radio. They were getting slightly better food than we were getting, and, after all, their relatives could visit them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now to the beatings at KP Dom. Were there beatings at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I remember, between the 1st and the 25th of June, 1992, quite a great deal of these facts came to light.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you first whether you could see a pattern in the way the beatings were conducted, and then I will ask you some specific questions about specific incidents. But first can you describe in general what the pattern was, how people were beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The criteria, conditions under which people were taken away for interviews and beatings, it's really difficult to say. We never managed to find that out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that people were taken away -- well, let me start asking you this way: Were detainees beaten immediately when they were brought into the KP Dom from the outside?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such instances, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us if you were able to see either the beatings themselves or the effects of the beatings?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not see, we could not see, because it happened at the entrance into the compound, but one could hear. After those men would be brought into the rooms, we could, of course, see that they had been beaten on various parts of their bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said you could hear, what could you hear?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard the cries of pain of those poor things, because they wailed and screamed, and one could hear the blows resound of some batons or something; especially, of course, it was particularly audible at night-time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were detainees who were brought in at night-time as well as daytime?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you hear these cries and blows coming from? Could you locate where they were?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that. It is in this entrance into the administrative building; that is, as soon as they would be brought there, they would be searched, I suppose, and harassment by perhaps people on duty or perhaps others who happened to be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before these individuals were brought to your room or to other prisoners' rooms, could you see them walking through the yard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You have to say yes rather than just nod, sir. It won't be recorded in the transcript otherwise. You just nodded in answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see happen to these individuals as they came through the yard?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We really saw one. He was a male nurse, and he was severely beaten on his legs and soles of his feet and his arms, around here, so he had difficulty moving. He even stumbled once; I mean, his legs simply wouldn't support him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anybody actually inflict blows in the yard?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people whose injuries you saw, did they explain to you how they received those injuries, who did it to them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At times it could not be said directly to me, for instance. But later on we moved between rooms and we communicated with those people, and they usually gave the names of those men who had beaten them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The men who had beaten these detainees on their way in, were they guards or soldiers, or what category of people were they?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Guards and representatives of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were detainees brought in from? What areas?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the town itself and its environs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there detainees brought in from particular areas who were singled out for beating, as far as you could tell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what criteria were applied to various citizens and villagers, but the fact remains that they were brought from the town and out of the town, and not only from the environs or the town itself but from other towns as well; not only from Bosnia-Herzegovina but even from other parts of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned one particular incident where a male nurse was brought in badly beaten, into your room. Can you give us some other specific incidents of who was beaten and how, when they first arrived at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can mention some people, some nurses and other individuals. Also, if you need the names, I can give them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please do so? Just tell us the specific incidents, who was beaten, and if you know by whom, and also when.

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you straight away that I do not know who beat them because that was right at the beginning, that is, early June. Enes Uzunovic is one of them, a prominent bloke. He was the president of the youth organisation and a male nurse. He was very badly beaten, harassed; transferred from one to another. Nisic Nurko, he was a lawyer. He worked for the municipal assembly. Alija Ugljesa, who was brought from Ilovaca. Ilovaca is in the municipality of Gorazde. Safet Minovic, from the municipality of Cajnice, who happened to be in the Foca hospital. Some policemen who were professional policemen in Foca, and many, many others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Kuo, are you able to assist us in the same way that your colleague did by giving us any references to the schedules to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm in the process of getting that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: For the record, Nurko Nisic is 19 on Schedule C, that's Exhibit P55. The person identified as Uzunovic is person 26 on the same Schedule C. And those are the only ones I can identify at the moment, Your Honour. We will ask this witness to look at Schedule C later and confirm all the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Not just Schedule C. There is an earlier one or a later one which has a series of incidents, particular incidents, not ones that ended up in Schedule C. If they are referred to by any of these witnesses, it does help if it's recorded in the transcript so that later it can be assembled far more easily.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I know the schedule you are referring to but I don't have it at hand. I will be able to provide it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you about another group or category of beatings. Were detainees taken out of rooms and beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this during the daytime or the night-time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both by day and by night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell if there was a difference between the beatings that occurred during the daytime and the ones that occurred in the night-time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see why the investigation would last in the -- by day and by night and the beatings and battery also happened by day and by night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the investigation would last in the day and by night, what investigation do you mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say really what they interviewed people about, what questions were about or why they were beaten. I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did guards come and take prisoners from the individual rooms?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they say why they were being taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They would only open the door to the room and call out a particular individual to come with them to the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What led you to believe that these detainees being taken out were being interviewed?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, they would come back, usually beaten, not always to the same room where they had been taken out. For some reason, they were sometimes transferred to some other rooms so that we would see them only a couple of days later and then they would tell you their impressions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The detainees who were brought back in this way, did they tell you what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they mostly insisted in coercing them to affirming that they were involved in some activities, that they were making some attempts, that they were trying to do something for the other side and things to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those detainees tell you who, and by "who", I don't mean necessarily individuals, but the category of people, again, soldiers, guards, or other people? Who was doing this kind of questioning and the beating?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in some parts, guards alone participated. At times, members of the military police would come to do that, and there were also some other men who were accommodated in -- allegedly, in the canteen of the KP Dom and who came there to conduct investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "accommodated in the canteen", what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those must have been representatives of some units who were engaged on such occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of units do you mean, military units or --

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reserve, I suppose reserve force of some units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, reserve forces of the military, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really say with any certainty whether the army of some special units. It's really difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, when you say they were accommodated at the canteen, did you mean they actually lived there or they used it for work purposes?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were staying there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually living there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell what relationship those people had with the prison guards? In other words, did they cooperate with each other, did they function separately or did they function together?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, together, I suppose, because it was in cooperation with the military command and, I suppose, the administration of the penitentiary of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many people were accommodated in the canteen in this way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they have beds there in the same place where detainees would eat?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because that is a building which, before the war, was a kind of a restaurant with an additional part on the upper floor where they had some rooms to let.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are referring to the rooms upstairs, that's where these reserve unit members were staying; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you some specific questions about specific incidents when detainees were taken out of their rooms and beaten. Do you recall specific individuals who were victimised in this way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we remember people who were taken away, who were brought back, and those who were not brought back. Because they were not brought back and they are still gone, we understand that they are still missing, that is either they were liquidated right there on the spot or would be taken somewhere else and liquidated there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to concentrate on the incidents when individuals were taken out and returned and you were able to see the injuries on them. Let's focus on those. Can you tell us about some of those incidents?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a number of those people and I can't recall all of those names, but I can remember some of them and the types of injuries and which parts of the body. Amir Berberkic was a physician in the general hospital. He was brought from his place of work in the hospital. He was beaten on the legs and it took him some time to recover with our help and some assistance of the medical personnel in the administration of the KP Dom. Alija Ugljesa had been severely beaten, and the guard Novica Burilo who weight some 100 kilograms jumped on him and broke several of his ribs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Berberkic tell you who had injured him, who had beat him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he never wanted to do that. I don't know why. Many people tried to keep it to themselves, perhaps afraid to divulge those names. Perhaps they also were told not to tell anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did either Dr. Berberkic or Alija Ugljesa tell you what happened during the beating, whether the people who were doing the beating said anything about why they were beating them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. It did not last long, the blows with some batons or kicks, that is with military boots. So that during that short period of time people screamed, yelled. I think it's not that I think, it's according to them, there were quite a number of them who would seize the opportunity to attack and beat them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "seize the opportunity", who were you talking about? Who was seizing the opportunity to beat?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that part where they took those people, that is this front part between the administration and the inside of the penitentiary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is who? Who took the opportunity to beat the detainees?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Guards. Guards. And those who happened to be there. Those who had invited them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the two individuals whose names you've mentioned, can you remember other individuals who were beaten in this way and brought back?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said so, Nurko Nisic, Halim Konjo, Enes Uzunovic. It's not easy to remember them just now, but there were quite a number of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a detainee in your room whose daughter was actually detained with him for a short period of time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a man whose name was Muharem Causevic with his three-year-old daughter. Around three, three and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was she detained there with him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really say, but I should say it was a lot more than a month, because he was one of those who was also taken out repeatedly and beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he taken out and beaten during the time that his daughter was there with him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he was returned from the beatings, could you see injuries on him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That Room 15 had two parts; a smaller part in which he was with five or six other prisoners and that other part where there were some 25 to 30 men. So I could not see him at the moment when he would come back, but a couple of days later, yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you observe about him during the time that you did see him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slaps and blows on the body, on various parts of the body. So a couple of days later, one could still see bruises, even though not that pronounced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times was he taken out while his daughter was there with him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, but two or three times, not less than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what would happen to his daughter when he was taken out and beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was with those men in the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the daughter? Did she stay?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day a prisoner came and said that she would be taken to her mother or relations, something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the person who has been described as Muharem Causevic is listed in Schedule A, incident 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. If you come across any others, perhaps you can let us know at some stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: We are trying to compile them as simultaneously as possible. Sometimes things come to light that we didn't have the details on earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When detainees were taken out and beaten, could those of you who stayed in the room hear the beatings? You need to say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the place where this was done and the place that we were at were about 30 to 40 metres away from one another, yes, you could hear that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the place where this was done, where the beatings were done, where was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually in this part that I'm talking about all the time, that is to say, this part between the administrative building and the entrance into the compound of the penitentiary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the same area as the entranceway, or would it have been an office in a different part of the building? I'm talking now about the beatings where detainees were taken out of the rooms and then brought back. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they did not return everyone to the same rooms. But this happened in the same rooms most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I'd like to have the witness shown Exhibit 6/1 so we can determine precisely what area he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please -- you mentioned the part of the building where the beatings were occurring. Where is that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, in this part.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The record should reflect that the witness is pointing to the area that is directly behind the entrance into the KP Dom as you enter. It appears to be an anteroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's, in fact, the area between the entrance to the KP Dom and the entrance from the interior, or the exit to the interior of the KP Dom which has been shown on these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely where this witness has indicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you tell if there was a pattern in the way the prisoners were taken out? In other words, were there lists from which the guards would call out names?

utterances.speaker: FWS-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some people were called out individually, but then there were also lists that were made up amongst us, the prisoners. Very often the prison guards would come into our rooms and compile a list of our names, and then they took them back to the administration people. Whether these were the criteria for taking people out, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
